messages:
sanjay: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak i started seeing intermittent OOMs during prefix-cache warmup on p4d. Not a constant fail but spikes at scale. Anyone else seeing this?

lisa: saw the same on canary. profile (perfetto link): https://perf.redwood/trace/58f3 — peak GPU alloc ~18.6GB vs 14.2GB before. looks like workspace allocations grew on some kernels.

tomas: possible explanation: new kernel path allocates separate workspace per batch instead of reusing the slab. batching heuristic also increased per-request seq_len to avoid fragmentation, which multiplies workspace.

sanjay: yep that matches the trace — multiple simultaneous small batches lead to N * workspace instead of pooled reuse. devbot fired an OOM alert at 02:14 UTC.

devbot: [ALERT] model-infer-1 OOM on node g-17a (pid 2419). recent deploy: kernel-select-v3. rollback candidate: kernel-select-v2.

abby: also seeing a lot of cold prefixes hitting the prefix cache during warmup. TTL is 48h, shard sizing 128MB default, leading to many small cold entries getting materialized then evicted. warmup traffic + larger workspace = compounding memory pressure.

kevin: ran a quick sim with 1M prefixes, TTL skewed towards short-lived sessions. baseline hit-rate 27% at 128MB shards. with 256MB shards hit-rate 33% but memory footprint jumps ~1.9x.

lisa: we need to decide: reduce per-kernel workspace or change cache shard policy (smaller shard, shorter TTL) or both. Any measurable knobs we can flip quickly for a canary?

tomas: quick knobs: enable workspace-pool-reuse=true, workspace-hardcap=8MB, batcher-max-inflight=32. Those should limit multiplicative allocation. also a fallback: kernel-select-v2 route on low-memory nodes.

sanjay: can we prototype a minimal change set and run a 20% canary? propose: (1) enable pool reuse, (2) set hardcap 8MB, (3) change prefixcache ttl from 48h -> 6h on canary, (4) bump shard to 192MB to trade a bit of memory for hit-rate stability.

kevin: i ran a quick micro-sim. numbers:
- baseline (no reuse, ttl48, shard128): peak mem 18.6GB, p99 latency 210ms, prefix-hit 27%
- reuse + hardcap8MB + ttl6 + shard192: peak mem 13.1GB, p99 latency 220ms, prefix-hit 31%
- only reuse+hardcap: peak 14.0GB, hit 28%
so reuse+caps address most of the OOM. ttl shrink reduces warmup churn further.

abby: nice. can we get a short config snippet for the canary so infra can apply?

tomas: sure — config to flip:
```
serving.runtime.workspace_pool_reuse = true
serving.runtime.workspace_hardcap_bytes = 8388608  # 8MB
serving.batcher.max_inflight = 32
prefixcache.shard_size_mb = 192
prefixcache.default_ttl_h = 6
route.override.kernel_select = "v2"  # fallback for low-memory nodes
```

lisa: add a feature-flag gate and roll to 20% traffic for 2h, watch OOMs, p99, and prefix-hit. also collect per-shard memory histograms.

sanjay: i'll coordinate the canary. tomas — can you run the regression harness (alloc-pressure suite) against kernel-select-v3+reuse so we have a repro before we flip? want a failing test in CI.

tomas: on it. i'll run with 10k synthetic sessions (mixed seq lengths) and attach logs. expect results in ~45m.

kevin: i'll prepare a short spreadsheet with the sim numbers and a quick script to sweep shard sizes + ttl to find knee points.

abby: action items:
- tomas: run alloc-pressure suite + post trace (ETA 45m)
- kevin: run shard/ttl sweep script and share knee chart (ETA 1h)
- sanjay/lisa: prepare canary rollout plan and feature-flag config (ETA 30m)

sanjay: thanks. goal is to keep kernel-select improvements but not regress production memory. if we can get workspace reuse + small caps + smarter TTL for warmup, we should be safe. ping here with traces and i'll shepherd the canary. :thumbsup:
